answer_1.quote: Many of the use cases addressed focus on summarization (e.g., news summarization or headline generation) and use popular news datasets for testing (CNN/DailyMail news articles corpus , or XSUM news headline dataset ).
answer_1.outputs: LLM responses in the form of summaries containing claims that are evaluated for hallucination against reference contexts.

answer_2.quote: We produce an aggregated hallucination score by measuring the rate of unsupported claims (i.e., those assigned classes other than supported), and calculate the distribution of fine-grained error types.

answer_3.quote: we use LLMs with prompt engineering for hallucination detection and measurement, achieving better performance.

answer_4.quote: Four researchers manually annotated the claims; each claim was annotated by two annotators, with disagreements adjudicated.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluated claims against the reference context to identify three main types and 10 specific types (i.e., subtypes) of hallucinations (Table ).
